articles.title: Nasdaq CEO flags IPO slowdown amid market volatility
articles.content: The IPO market is grappling with hurdles stemming from macroeconomic instability and fluctuating market conditions that are influencing corporate strategies. Numerous firms have either delayed or abandoned their public listing intentions lately. Nevertheless, Nasdaq maintains a sturdy and vibrant pipeline for future listings, even as analysts caution that a revival in IPO activity likely won't materialize until 2026 without a surge in investor interest.

articles.title: This Tata Group stock plunged 10% a day after rallying 19% post Q2 results. Do you own?
articles.content: Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) shares plunged on Friday, giving up some gains after rallying 19% in the previous session following its Q2 results. The stock fell to Rs 34.24 on the NSE. The company reported a net loss of Rs 59 crore in Q2 FY27, narrowing from Rs 321 crore a year earlier and Rs 72 crore in the previous quarter. Despite the improvement, the stock has declined over 30% in 2026 so far and 59% in three years.

articles.title: Cyient shares rally 9% after Q2 revenue rises 25%; board declares Rs 12/sh interim dividend

Safe-haven demand pushes Japan’s 10-year yield to two-month low
articles.content: Japanese government bonds saw a rally on Friday, leading to the benchmark 10-year yield hitting a two-month low. articles.title: Christopher Wood swapped Nvidia for a Greek infrastructure stock. The bet is paying off
articles.content: Jefferies’ Christopher Wood replaced Nvidia with Greek infrastructure company GEK TERNA in his global long-only equity portfolio in October 2025. Since then, GEK TERNA has gained 65% in US-dollar terms, compared with Nvidia’s 15%. The shift reflects Wood’s preference for infrastructure, fiscal reform and improving economic fundamentals over crowded AI trades.

articles.title: Rs 9,000 crore wiped out in a day: Why Swiggy investors are losing patience with Instamart
articles.content: Swiggy shares plunged on Friday, wiping out around ₹9,000 crore in market value as widening Instamart losses overshadowed food delivery growth. Following Q2 results, brokerages cut their price targets, citing deteriorating quick-commerce profitability. Instamart’s adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹895 crore from ₹778 crore, while its contribution margin deteriorated to -1.4% despite 13.4% sequential growth in net order value.

articles.title: Bansal Wire Industries Q2 net profit jumps 38% to Rs 53 crore
articles.content: Bansal Wire Industries reported a remarkable consolidated net profit of Rs 52.9 crore for the quarter ending in September, marking a substantial 38 percent growth compared to the previous year. The company's revenue surged by 23.9 percent, amounting to Rs 1,308.1 crore for the same period. Sales volume also experienced a 12.4 percent increase, reaching 1.29 LT, while both EBITDA and EBITDA per tonne achieved record highs this quarter.

articles.title: Hindustan Zinc shares drop 4% as India allows large silver imports despite weak demand
articles.content: Hindustan Zinc shares fell sharply on Friday after India issued permits to import 6,500 metric tonnes of silver over the next six months to meet festive-season demand. The move could ease domestic premiums amid weak demand, while silver futures declined around 3%. The stock is down over 18% so far in 2026.

articles.title: ETMarkets Smart Talk: Smallcap investors should consider a five-year SIP horizon amid volatility: Sorbh Gupta
articles.content: In an interview with Kshitij Anand of ETMarkets, Sorbh Gupta, Head of Equity at Bajaj Asset Management Limited, says investors considering smallcap exposure could look at a five-year SIP horizon, depending on their risk appetite and financial goals.
